Solution 8 (most simple, easy, estimation)[edit]

First, let's test what happens if . If , the area of the circle around each lattice point is . Since each lattice point corresponds to a square of area, the probability of the point falling within units is exactly . Because this strictly exceeds our target probability of , we know that . This conveniently eliminates and , and proves that the circles centered at the lattice points do not overlap.

Since the circles do not overlap, we can simply find the combined favorable area of the circles (and partial circles) inside the square.

We can break this down into three types of lattice points: There are interior lattice points, each contributing a full circle of area . There are edge lattice points (excluding corners), each contributing a semicircle of area . There are corner lattice points, each contributing a quarter-circle of area .
